column1: # Combat's damage vocabulary. `combat.md` Section 11 publishes the resolution
# words - the miss, the graze, the hit, the wound grades and the two overkill
# descriptions - and `scenario_literal_coverage.py` reports that not one of
# them has ever appeared in a sampled stock frame.
# This is a lottery by construction and is marked as one so the comparator
# does not score the dice: the two sides roll independently, so the word one
# prints on a given swing is not the word the other prints. What it is for is
# the *vocabulary* - which words the original draws from, in what shape, and
# on which row - which a run of swings surfaces on both sides even when no
# The seat is the town attack, not the dungeon room: the room the dungeon
# seed enters is empty, so every swing there answers `Attack-Aim!` and
# `Nothing!` and no damage word is reachable at all. Attacking the
# weaponsmith opens an arena that actually has a foe in it.
# The foe is not adjacent on entry - it stands four cells north - and bare
# hands are `combat.md §8.2`'s zero-reach arm, whose cursor cannot leave the
# cells within range. So the party walks north first and only then swings;
# the earlier form of this scenario pressed `a` from the entry cell and
# collected six `Nothing!` answers instead. Those answers did earn their
# keep: they found the missing line feeds around `Nothing!`, which is fixed.
# requires-seed: the party beside the weaponsmith in a town
